page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the t3a.xlarge is positioned in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 154.73 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 11.7 GB/sec. However, the CPU demonstrates average performance in PassMark encryption tests, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA_NI instructions. Static web serving throughput is recorded at 2.73 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations reach 2.53 million operations per second.

Given its burstable CPU allocation model and older AMD EPYC hardware, the t3a.xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with variable or spike-prone CPU utilization. The burstable model allows users to pay a lower baseline rate while retaining the ability to burst to full CPU performance when needed, though sustained high-compute tasks will deplete CPU credits and face performance throttling. This resource profile is best suited for low-traffic web servers, development environments, small databases, and background microservices that do not require continuous high-performance compute or local storage.
